card.band: 4 h. A frontier agent usually finds the loser tree and gets part of the speedup. The remaining gains need stride-based key layout and a cache-friendly design. A weaker model stays near the baseline.
card.cheat: Caching results or skipping the merge: the inputs are hidden and fresh per run, and equality is checked on the full stream.
card.grading: Hard gate: output equal to the baseline on a generated hidden set of runs (duplicates, ties, nulls, varied k from 2 to 4096). Reward from the wall-clock median speedup over several k and key-width cases against our reference speedup.
card.reference: The upstream merged PR (about 600 lines), whose measured speedup defines S. Measured by us in the container.
card.task: /app ships the pre-PR Druid merge code, an isolated Java module for sorted-run and row-iterator k-way merging, with a build and a microbenchmark harness. The agent keeps behaviour identical and makes merging of many sorted runs faster, for example with a tournament/loser tree and compact key strides.
card.title: Druid k-way merge speedup via tournament trees

source_notes: repo https://github.com/apache/druid; merged PR or fixed issue

facts.claim: Druid PR #15661 exists and is merged: 'Faster k-way merging using tournament trees, 8-byte key strides', merged 2024-01-11, merge commit 2231cb30a4d76244c1f81ce71ff73120b5e99cd2

PR changes the k-way merge in processing/frame (FrameChannelMerger, new TournamentTree, FrameComparisonWidgetImpl, FrameReaderUtils) with a new FrameChannelMergerBenchmark; the seed's 'isolated Java module' description does not match this
PR is 5 commits touching 7 Java files; benchmark file adds 353 lines; the total added code is about 600 lines
Seed's 'pre-PR parent commit' is pinned: source_facts head d61f8cf93527d914d0750b3c06a7a24162bf5830 is the current master HEAD (pushed 2026-10-20), and the parent SHA of PR 15661 is not stated
Row-iterator k-way merging is part of the upstream PR
PR's own benchmark (5M rows, 20-char keys): 2 channels 662.988 -> 602.409 ms/op (1.10x); 16 channels 1513.897 -> 943.311 ms/op (1.60x) for tree plus 8-byte stride
Tag druid-38.0.0 exists, marked Latest, published 1 Oct (year not shown), so the later release already contains this code path
Druid 38.0.0 release notes: over 250 changes from 37 contributors, Java 25 support, Java 17 dropped
Repository is Apache-2.0 and not a fork, not archived (taken from the GitHub API facts supplied)

full_card.band: 4 h tier. Frontier finds the tournament tree (about 1.3x at 16 channels by the PR's own numbers) and must add stride key layout for the rest; weaker model stays near baseline (not verified).
full_card.build_cost: 3-4 days: extract the module from frame code, make it build offline, write the sealed grader and baseline, and calibrate the speedup.
full_card.deliverable: A standalone Java k-way merge (sorted runs and key compare) that is output-identical to the baseline and faster, with a benchmark harness.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Hidden inputs fresh per run, so caching fails; full-stream equality so skipping the merge fails; grader uses its own harness and baseline outside /app.
full_card.grading_surface: Generated hidden runs: duplicates, ties, nulls, k from 2 to 4096, varied key widths; full output stream equality as the gate; speedup as wall-clock median.
full_card.local_fit: Java 8-core CPU, offline; Druid Maven build must be made offline-buildable with pre-fetched deps, and the 437 MB repo is too big to ship whole.
full_card.lookup: direct: the PR is public and its design is named in the task text.
full_card.provenance: Upstream apache/druid PR #15661 merged 2024-01-11 (merge commit 2231cb3); Apache-2.0; public git history contains the reference.
full_card.reference: Upstream merged PR 15661 (TournamentTree plus 8-byte key strides); PR's own bench gives 1.10x at 2 channels and 1.60x at 16 channels.
full_card.ships: Druid processing and benchmark code at the pre-PR parent as a history-less snapshot, with no later release jars or sources and no ~/.m2 copy of newer druid-processing. Not an isolated module today; the agent or the task must extract a standalone merge module with a defined API.
full_card.similarity: Nearest seeds S-op-042 (0.241), S-op-041 (0.217), S-im-037 (0.207); no public task neighbour above 0.15 and not crowded.

Band.why: Seed's band is plausible but unverified; PR numbers (1.6x at 16 channels) suggest a frontier agent with the tree gets much of S; no dated public evidence.

Build.why: Module extraction from Druid frame code, offline build and sealed grader cost roughly 3-4 days.

Fit.why: Java CPU offline is fine, but a Maven build from a huge repo needs offline dependency pre-fetch.

Hor.why: About 400-600 lines of real work in a 4 h tier; too short for 8 h, so tier fits but scope is modest.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 permits shipping the source and reference.

Multi.why: Two levers (tree, strides) and k/key-width buckets; little independent surface.

Nov.why: Neighbours are seeds, not public tasks; no public task neighbour above 0.15.

Real.why: Merged upstream PR with a public number trail, release tag and benchmark numbers.

Ref.why: Measured upstream speedup defines S; a complete implementation exists.

Seal.why: Public history must be stripped and later release code excluded; agent can recall the design, which is a Band issue.

Surf.why: Generated differential runs against a baseline oracle with an unlimited generator.

spike_plan.kill_if: Speedup at 16 channels is under 1.2x or varies by more than 20% across repeats, or the offline build cannot be made to work without network.
spike_plan.pass_if: Parent SHA is pinned, the offline build works, speedups reproduce within about 10%, and output equality holds across k and key widths.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone apache/druid, record the parent SHA of 2231cb3 and check out that parent.
Build processing and the benchmarks module with Maven, pre-fetching dependencies; record whether the build works offline afterwards.
Run FrameChannelMergerBenchmark at the parent, and at 2231cb3, at 2 and 16 channels, with 3 repeats each; confirm the ratios are near 1.10x and 1.60x and the noise is small.
Write a 50-line harness that generates random sorted runs with duplicates, ties and nulls at k=2 and k=4096, and checks that the parent output equals the merged output on the full stream.
Check determinism: rerun the same seed three times and confirm identical output hashes and stable timing medians.

v1.summary: The upstream reference is real and merged (Druid PR #15661, Jan 2024), but the seed misstates its shape: it is not an isolated module, the parent SHA is not pinned (the head given is current master), and the 600-line size is unverified. The design is public and named in the task, so lookup is direct and the task only works with a history-less snapshot that excludes later release code, with an API the spec defines; the card is not killed, but the spike must confirm the speedup and the offline build before it goes further.
